q: By January 10, 2027, the United States and China again extend both the tariff truce and China's suspension of its rare-earth export controls, or replace them with a longer-term agreement
basis: On September 24, 2026, the United States and China extended their tariff truce by two months and put off the core issues (tariffs, rare earths, and technology controls). The U.S. Russia sanctions law (the Graham Act), which took effect on September 18, mandates tariffs from October 18 on major buyers of Russian oil and gas and could have collided with the truce had China been targeted, but President Trump waived those tariffs on October 16. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the president would review the effects for up to 60 days · Grand strategy: AI concentrates value in a few hubs and turns those hubs into targets On November 9, China's Commerce Ministry extended its suspension of export controls on rare earths and other materials by two months, to January 10, 2027; Reuters reported that this was part of a wider extension of China's suspension of trade countermeasures and tariffs announced the same day.
rs: Announcements by the White House or USTR and by China's Ministry of Commerce
